insights.claim: odh-model-controller deploys as two separate workloads (operator controller and REST API server) with distinct service accounts and RBAC scopes, creating a least-privilege boundary between controller reconciliation and user-facing API operations.
insights.reasoning: The analyzer identifies two Deployment workloads (odh-model-controller and model-serving-api) with separate service accounts. Source inspection confirms the model-serving-api has a narrower ClusterRole (gateway list + namespace get) compared to the controller's 36-rule ClusterRole, implementing least-privilege separation between operator logic and user-facing API surface.

insights.claim: The controller dynamically adapts TLS configuration from the OpenShift cluster-wide TLS profile and triggers a graceful restart when the profile changes, ensuring runtime compliance with cluster security policy.
insights.reasoning: The pkg/tls package reads apiservers.config.openshift.io/cluster at startup and resolves cipher suites and minimum TLS version. The ProfileWatcher controller watches for changes and triggers a graceful shutdown, ensuring the operator always serves with the current cluster-wide TLS policy. This pattern is significant for platform operators who need assurance that component TLS follows cluster policy changes.

insights.claim: The Konflux build enforces FIPS cryptography via GOEXPERIMENT=strictfipsruntime with dynamic linking, and the application-level cipher suite configuration exclusively uses FIPS-approved algorithms.
insights.reasoning: The build uses strictfipsruntime (both GOEXPERIMENT and build tag), which enforces that all Go crypto operations use the FIPS-validated OpenSSL backend. The application TLS configuration only includes ECDHE ciphers with AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, all FIPS 140-2/140-3 approved. This dual enforcement (build-time and application-level) provides defense-in-depth for FIPS compliance.
